version.changelog: Security hardening: privacy consent, path consistency, permission declaration, SkillHub frontmatter

llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed session-handoff helper that reads project context and writes a handoff document, with consent gates for more sensitive IDE profile scans.

dimensions.detail: The requested capabilities fit the stated purpose: analyze the current coding session/project, generate a structured handoff document, and produce a startup prompt for a new conversation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The trigger phrases are short and broad, but the artifact clearly frames them as user invocation examples and requires warning the user before file writing plus explicit consent before IDE-specific identity, memory, or configuration scanning.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The package contains Markdown skill instructions and reference templates only; no executable scripts, install hooks, subprocess use, or external API integration are present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Project file reads and handoff-file writes are proportionate for the purpose. IDE-specific WorkBuddy identity/memory/config scans are more sensitive, but they are disclosed and gated on explicit user consent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill persists a generated handoff file and may overwrite the configured handoff path. It instructs agents not to store secrets, token values, real names, emails, or absolute user paths, but users should review the generated document before reuse.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you want an agent to create or overwrite a session handoff file in your project. Review the generated handoff before pasting it into a new conversation, and decline IDE-specific scanning unless you are comfortable sharing WorkBuddy/Cursor/TRAE/Claude rules, memory, identity, task, or connector metadata for continuity.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The broad trigger phrases are real, but they are disclosed as usage examples for a handoff workflow. Because the file write is expected and disclosed, this is a usability caution rather than a Review-level concern.
[SQP-3] expected: Recording communication language is part of continuity handoff and is low sensitivity. The broader template also includes personal-information filtering, so this does not support escalation, though users can omit preferences they do not want persisted.
